finds.title: Publish and photograph the weekday lunch bento
finds.summary: Your lunch specials and bentos already get named in reviews but are barely visible online — put them on the website and Google with photos and prices to win the midday walk-in…
finds.rationale: Two separate sources point at lunch as an underworked strength: a diner reports lunch specials at roughly $10-11 per entree (6ad117f0), and a Yelp regular specifically praises the lunch bentos and calls the place right for a casual daytime visit (09c1515f). You open at 11:30 every day (91248c4e, 752c1172), so the lunch window is already staffed and paid for. But the online presence gives a browsing visitor no lunch price, no bento photo and no reason to choose you at noon — the listings show only casual dining and a $30-and-under band (d63f1161, 13631a55). Daytime on this stretch is dominated by cafes and quick counters; a proper sit-down Japanese lunch with a view has no direct competitor in that slot. Making the lunch offer findable is a listings job, not a kitchen job.
finds.move:
Write out the weekday lunch bento and special menu with current prices.
Photograph three bentos on the patio in daylight.
Add a dedicated lunch section to the website with those prices and photos.
Upload the lunch photos to Google Business Profile and Yelp.
Post the lunch menu as a Google Post once a week.
Track midday covers separately for four weeks.
Confirm the prices with the owner before anything goes live.

finds.title: Fix delivery value: add a fixed-price sushi set
finds.summary: Delivery reviewers are complaining about portion size for the price, so add one clearly-described fixed-price set and steer repeat orders to your commission-free Toast page.
finds.rationale: The delivery reviews split hard on value, not on taste: one guest paid $51 for three rolls and called it nowhere near the value, another paid $32 for a sushi sampler and was unhappy (390cc17d). Meanwhile the same listing shows a la carte rolls at $21.95 to $23.95 (91248c4e) and entrees from $23 to $54.95 (390cc17d), so a customer assembling an order has no way to feel they got a deal. A single named, photographed set at a fixed price with the piece count stated removes the guesswork and resets the value impression — this is the cheapest fix available because it is a menu-description change, not a discount. Your Toast page is commission free and money goes straight to you (91248c4e), so every order you move off the marketplaces is worth materially more per dollar than a delivery order.
finds.move:
Build one fixed-price sushi set for two with the exact piece count written into the description.
Photograph it as it actually leaves the kitchen in a takeout box.
List the set at the top of the Toast ordering page and on the third-party menus.
Add a card in every delivery bag pointing to the Toast page as the direct-order option.
Check the packed portion against the photo for the first two weeks.
Get owner approval on the set contents and price before launch.

finds.title: Lead every listing with the ocean-view patio
finds.summary: Your patio view is the thing guests rave about, but your website and delivery listings sell takeout instead — put the view front and centre to pull in visitors and date-night…
finds.rationale: Review after review names the same asset: the patio, the ocean breeze, the 'million dollar view' (ddbcdc49), 'excellent food, great view, sit on the ocean view terrace' (7918693f), and diners who say they come 'less for the food and more for the view... perfect for a casual brunch or low key date' (09c1515f, c8c1e6c4). Yet the website copy is entirely about sushi, delivery and takeout with no mention of the patio or the ocean at all (38bffe87, d1427ddc), and the Yelp photo set leads with food shots rather than the terrace (09c1515f). Every high-traffic rival on this stretch of coast — the cafe, the resort restaurants — wins visitors on view. You have the same asset and are not claiming it. This is a copy-and-photo change with no food cost and no new labour, aimed squarely at the visitor and tourist segment you already say you serve.
finds.move:
Replace the top line of the website homepage with a sentence naming the ocean-view patio.
Shoot six good daylight photos of the patio with the ocean behind it.
Set a patio photo as the primary image on Google Business Profile, Yelp and the Toast ordering page.
Add 'Outdoor seating' and 'Great view' attributes on the Google profile.
Add one line to the Google Business description mentioning the ocean-view terrace.
Get owner sign-off on the wording before publishing.
